newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian 96/97 sugarcane output seen at 271.87 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Indian 96/97 sugarcane output seen at 271.87 mln T.

text.p: India's sugarcane output in 1996/97 (April-March) is forecast at 271.87 million tonnes compared to 282.95 million in 1995/96, United News of India (UNI) quoted Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav as saying on Tuesday.
The government is actively considering delicensing the sugar industry, UNI quoted Yadav as saying.
India has abolished licences for many industries as part of sweeping economic reforms launched in 1991. But it has maintained its grip over the sugar industry.
Production and pricing of sugar are currently controlled by the government.

The mills supply 40 percent of their output as levy at a subsidised rate for distribution among the poor. The government controls the release of the remainder on the free market through the use of sales quotas.
In August, the government ended the monopoly held by a private company, set up by the sugar millers, over exports.
Industry officials since then have demanded the deregulation of sugar prices, a move which they say would enhance efficiency and boost exports at competitive prices.
